verdict: VICI's rent and financing income grew 5.8% to $1.07B and its cash-style AFFO rose 7.5%, but a $458M non-cash credit-loss allowance charge cut GAAP net income to $347M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.71 a year ago — hit by the CECL charge

segments.name: Sales-type lease income
segments.note: Rent from casino resorts leased directly to operators — Caesars, the MGM Grand/Mandalay Bay and Venetian leases are the biggest pieces.

segments.name: Financing, loans & securities
segments.note: Income from lease financing receivables (led by the MGM master lease), plus interest on loans and securities the company holds.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Other income, fully offset by matching other expenses below — it does not add to profit.

segments.name: Golf revenues
segments.note: Revenue from the company's golf courses.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — remarkably lean for a landlord of this size.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Expenses that exactly offset the other income above.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: A small charge — most of VICI's assets are leases and loans, not buildings it depreciates.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $215M on the company's debt, partly offset by $2M of interest income.

takeaways.title: The rent roll keeps growing
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 5.8% to $1.07B, with built-in rent escalators doing most of the work — the triple-net model means tenants pay the property costs, not VICI.

takeaways.title: A paper charge sank GAAP profit
takeaways.text: The change in the CECL allowance — a non-cash reserve against lease and loan receivables — swung from a $20M release a year ago to a $458M charge, cutting net income attributable to common stockholders by 55% to $343M.

takeaways.title: The cash measure grew anyway
takeaways.text: AFFO, which adds the non-cash charge back, rose 7.5% to $685M, and management raised full-year AFFO guidance to $2,695M–$2,705M.

oneTimers: A $458M non-cash increase in the allowance for credit losses (CECL) — versus a $20M release in the same quarter last year. It is the sole reason GAAP net income fell 55%; AFFO excludes it.
footerNote: For this landlord-lender, the change in the allowance for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue — a non-cash reserve that AFFO adds back. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $343M ($0.31 per share).
